Here’s a quick recipe you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or your favourite HTTP client) to pull only the **ID** and **context** fields for the CAA records of `sample2.com`.  
Just replace the placeholder `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with your real key (`secret567`) when you run it.

```bash
curl -X GET \
     "https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/caa_records?fields=id,context" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
     -H "Accept: application/json"
```

### What this does

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `GET https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/caa_records` | Fetches the list of CAA records for the domain. |
| `?fields=id,context` | Tells the API to return *only* the `id` and `context` properties for each record. |
| `Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>` | Authenticates the request with your API key. |
| `Accept: application/json` | Requests the response in JSON format. |

### Expected response

```json
{
  "records": [
    {
      "id": "caasample2com-001",
      "context": {
        "issue": "letsencrypt.org",
        "iodef": "mailto:security@example.com"
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "caasample2com-002",
      "context": {
        "issuewild": "digicert.com",
        "iodef": "mailto:certs@example.com"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

If your provider supports pagination, you may also add `page=1&per_page=50` (or whatever limits you prefer) to the query string.  

That’s all you need—no extra headers, no body payload, just a clean GET request that returns exactly the two fields you asked for. Happy querying!
